flags.title: Two official population series disagree for the same year
flags.finding: For 2025 the DOF P-2A series has Los Angeles County at 9,853,435 and the Census Bureau V2025 estimate is 9,694,934, a gap of 158,501 people (+1.6% of the Census figure). The 2020 base also differs by source: DOF P-2A 10,012,050; Census 2020 count 10,014,009; Census V2025 estimate base 10,017,414 (the last two as shown in the QuickFacts excerpt).
flags.action: Choose one series per analysis, state its vintage, and never splice DOF and Census values in one trend line.

flags.title: EDD county and state projection windows differ
flags.finding: The county file covers 2023-2033 (published April 2026); the California file listed on the same page covers 2024-2034. EDD also warns that projections for previous periods are not always comparable to the latest.
flags.action: Do not compare the county percentage with the state percentage. Compare only within one file.

flags.title: County projection moved about 10% in five years; the path check is illustrative, not a validated back-test
flags.finding: An LAUSD analyst quoting DOF's May 2019 projection said Los Angeles County would reach about 10.8 million by 2030. DOF's current baseline has 9,727,305 for 2030. The 2019 path also projected small gains for 2021 to 2024 while DOF's current series shows a decline over 2020 to 2024. Limits: the 2019 figure is second-hand and rounded; the 'observed' series is DOF's own current estimate (revised), not an independent count; there are only five annual points.
flags.action: Use this only as a warning about forecast error. A true back-test needs the original 2019 DOF file and an independent observed series, and should not be claimed until both are in hand.

flags.title: Tenant-brand FY2026 results not yet published
flags.finding: Jack in the Box reports fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results on 2026-12-09, so the series on the Peers page ends at Q3 FY2026 and the Q4 row is blank. This is a decision input that arrives in about two weeks.
flags.action: Do not commit to a sale or renewal before reading the 2026-12-09 release. Extend the series afterwards (suggestion SUG-1).

flags.title: Metro D Line Sections 2 and 3 opening dates are not stated
flags.finding: The official project page says Sections 2 and 3 are under construction and gives no opening date. A non-official encyclopedia page states a year; it is not used.
flags.action: Leave blank until Metro states a date.

flags.title: Fast food wage: only the statute text was seen; current rate and the Council's end date are unconfirmed
flags.finding: The bill text excerpt states $20 per hour effective 2024-04-01 and describes the Council as lasting until 2029-01-01 'or as otherwise provided'. The DIR Fast Food Council page could not be fetched, and later amendments were not checked. Some non-official sites claim there is no later rate; they are not used.
flags.action: Confirm on the DIR page and in current Labor Code text before using any wage figure in a model.

flags.title: FEMA flood data services returned HTTP 500
flags.finding: Two forms of the National Flood Hazard Layer service URL failed, and other sessions logged the same for the Map Service Center. Automated flood-zone lookup is therefore not enabled.
flags.action: Use the FEMA Map Service Center by hand for the real parcel, and keep the result private.

flags.title: An older CAL FIRE service is not safe to automate
flags.finding: The services.gis.ca.gov fire severity service lists State Responsibility Area layers dated 2007 and DRAFT Local Responsibility Area layers. Using it could return a stale zone label.
flags.action: Use the official State Fire Marshal map viewer by hand and record the map date.

flags.title: Census data needs a key; one Census documentation page could not be opened
flags.finding: The Census Data API now returns a 'Missing Key' notice without a key. The TIGERweb REST documentation page could not be fetched. The private workflow therefore uses the public Gazetteer file for tract choice and takes the API key from an environment variable.
flags.action: Request a free key; never commit it or paste it into a pull request.

flags.title: Property-tax decline-in-value window closes Monday 2026-11-30
flags.finding: The Assessor's annual window is July 2 to November 30. Whether any claim fits is unknown because assessed value and January 1 market value are not known here, and the lease decides who controls appeals.
flags.action: Ask the property-tax adviser this week whether a filing makes sense; otherwise let the date pass knowingly.
